'''Angelita Castro Kelly''' (born '''Angelita Albano Castro''', August 26, 1942 - June 7, 2015) was a space scientist<ref name="ABS Obit">{{cite news |title=Filipina who dreamed big: Space scientist Angelita Castro-Kelly, 73 |url=https://www.abs-cbn.com/global-filipino/06/17/15/filipina-who-dreamed-big-space-scientist-angelita-castro-kelly-73 |access-date=27 August 2020 |work=ABS-CBN News |publisher=ABS-CBN Corporation |date=17 June 2015 |language=en}}</ref> and physicist.<ref name="Thomas Varsitarian Bio">{{cite news |last1=Santos |first1=Tomas U. |title=US space 'hero' is a Thomasian alumna |url=http://varsitarian.net/news/20081117/us_space_hero_is_a_thomasian_alumna |accessdate=27 August 2020 |publisher=The Varsitarian |date=17 November 2008}}</ref> She is the first female Mission Operations Manager (MOM) of [[NASA]]. She spearheaded and supervised the [[Earth Observing System]] missions during its developmental stage.<ref name="PhilStar NASA Job">{{cite news |title=Fil-Am mom gets NASA medal |url=https://www.philstar.com/other-sections/the-good-news/2010/08/01/598202/fil-am-mom-gets-nasa-medal |accessdate=26 August 2020 |work=philstar.com |publisher=PhilStar Global Corp. |date=1 August 2020}}</ref>

Castro was born in [[Jones, Isabela|Jones]], [[Isabela (province)|Isabela]] in 1942,<ref name="Filipina Womens Net Obit">{{cite news |title=In Memoriam: Dr. Angelita Castro-Kelly, U.S. FWN100™ '07, NASA'S Fearless Filipina Diplomat |url=https://filipinawomensnetwork.org/epahayagan/dr-angelita-castro-kelly-us-fwn100-07-passes#:~:text=credit%3A%20illustradolife.com-,Dr.,pharmacist%20Eufemia%20Albano%20and%20Dr. |accessdate=27 August 2020 |work=Filipina Women's Network |publisher=The Filipina Women’s Network |date=15 June 2015}}</ref> but she grew up in [[Sampaloc, Manila|Sampaloc]], [[Manila]]. Her mother was pharmacist Eufemia Albano and her father was Dr. Miguel Castro, who served as Captain of [[United States Army Forces in the Far East]] until he was killed in [[World War II]]. She was the youngest of seven children.<ref name="PhilStar NASA Job" />

When she moved to the US to pursue her education, she met fellow physicist Dr. Francis Kelly whom she eventually married.<ref name="Thomas Varsitarian Bio" />

==Education==
Castro was reportedly very active in school activities, such as debates, quizzes, contests, and student organizations.<ref name="Thomas Varsitarian Bio" /> In 1962, she acquired a bachelor's degree in Mathematics and Physics at the [[University of Santo Tomas]] where she graduated summa cum laude. Afterwards, she moved to the US to further her education. She obtained a master's degree in physics from the [[University of Maryland]].<ref name="Illustrado B">{{cite news |last1=Yap |first1=Abby |title=Angelita Castro-Kelly: NASA's Fearless Filipina Diplomat |url=http://illustradolife.com/angelita-castro-kelly-nasas-fearless-filipina-diplomat/ |accessdate=27 August 2020 |work=Illustrado Magazine - Filipino Abroad |publisher=Illustrado Magazine |date=6 September 2012}}</ref>

==NASA==
Castro worked at NASA for 37 years, from 1977 to 2015. In 1977, she began as a data analyst of the team that planned and executed the [[Goddard Space Flight Center]] (GSFC) Spacelab Data Processing Facility (SLDPF). The SPDF is a core space shuttle mission that aims to investigate [[microgravity]], [[solar physics]], crystal growth, and other scientific inquiries.<ref name="Thomas Varsitarian Bio" />
In 1990, she became the first female Mission Operations Manager of the [[Earth Observing System]] (EOS) project. It was a vital constituent of the Earth Science Enterprise program of NASA. She supervised the developmental stage of the three EOS missions: [[Terra (satellite)|terra]], aqua, and aura. Castro developed the operations concept of EOS, containing the EOS memoranda, among others. It became the basis of all EOS missions.<ref name="PhilStar NASA Job" />
Half of her 12 years service to NASA, she served a dual role as she also became the Earth Science Constellation Manager.<ref name="PhilStar NASA Job" />

Working in a room full of men, Castro recounted initially experiencing hostility from a few coworkers until she garnered their trust and respect by showing she is as adept and capable.<ref name="Illustrado B" />

==Death==
Castro suffered [[lupus]] until she succumbed to its complications on June 7, 2015. She was 73.<ref name="Yahoo News">{{cite news |title=First Pinay exec at NASA succumbs to lupus |url=https://ph.news.yahoo.com/first-pinay-exec-nasa-succumbs-160000681.html |accessdate=27 August 2020 |work=ph.news.yahoo.com |publisher=Yahoo News |language=en-PH}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2006, Castro was granted the Goddard Space Flight Center Exceptional Service Award.<ref name="Filipina Womens Net Obit" /> In 2007, 2008, and 2009, she received the [[NASA Exceptional Achievement Medal]]. She is also a recipient of the Austronauts' Manned Flight Program Launch Honoree, Astronauts’ Manned Flight “Snoopy” Award, Flight Project's “Mission Impossible” award, GSFC Exceptional Performance Award, and NASA Honor Group Achievement Award for the Constellation Mission Operations Working Group.<ref name="Illustrado B" /> In 2013, Castro received NASA's Outstanding Leadership Medal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013 |title=2013 Agency Honor Awards |url=https://searchpub.nssc.nasa.gov/servlet/sm.web.Fetch/2013_Agency_Honor_Awards_Brochure.pdf?rhid=1000&did=1626944&type=released |url-status=live |access-date=November 4, 2026 |publisher=National Aeronautics and Space Administration}}</ref>
